To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) RT-PCR analysis of peripheral blood from MM patients with localized or metastatic disease is a sensitive tool in detecting tumor cells; (ii) RT-PCR-positive peripheral blood is correlated with the risk of recurrence; (iii) RT-PCR is a sensitive method for detection of MM cells in histologically negative lymph nodes; (iv) RT-PCR results are currently being correlated to the patient's clinical status.
RT-PCR analysis for the presence of mRNA markers in peripheral and nodal samples from MM patients may provide useful prognostic information.
the presence of PCR-positive mRNA in peripheral blood is correlated to tumor burden and that molecular screening of tumor-negative nodes is feasible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a molecular marker profile for each MM patient, which could help clinicians to identify the risk of relapse in early stages of disease and to monitor disease progression.
the clinical significance of RT-PCR-positive markers in MM patients and with the potential role of RT- PCR as a monitoring tool for these patients.
the identification of a molecular marker for the early detection of MM metastasis and the development of an effective strategy for monitoring the disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of mRNA markers is a significant predictor of tumor burden in patients with MM.
PCR-positive mRNA markers are highly correlated with tumor burden, and may be useful as a prognostic marker in MM patients.
PCR with multiple markers is a useful and sensitive tool in the management of MM patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the detection of mRNA markers in blood and lymph nodes of MM patients has a prognostic value in predicting the risk of disease progression.

RT-PCR is a sensitive tool to identify MM cells in the peripheral blood and in histologically proven negative lymph nodes, and that the number of PCR markers correlates with the clinical status of the patient.

the presence of PCR-positive markers in the peripheral blood of MM patients is significantly associated with tumor burden, and the detection of these markers in tumor-negative lymph nodes is a reliable marker of occult metastases.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RT-PCR can be used to detect circulating MM cells and to evaluate tumor progression.
RT-PCR with multiple markers is a sensitive tool to assess the presence of tumor cells in peripheral blood and in regional lymph nodes of MM patients.
the detection of PCR-positive markers in the blood of MM patients may have a prognostic significance.
